L1 is not deleted and cannot be used as current guidance until revalidated.
C2 does not become verified team policy merely because C1 was retracted.

Child requests remain deferred and history coverage remains partial.

evals.prompt: Run the four-pass onboarding coordinator on supplied synthetic sources, not the host repository. Use ordinary agent dispatch, not native Workflow. Budget: eight actual worker launches, global concurrency three, logical depth two. Pass 1: launch independent product/component (S1,S4), culture/skills (C sources), and deployment (S2,S3) discovery nodes in one parallel batch where supported; withhold H history and F follow-up sources. Validate the map gate. Pass 2: derive two component workers, ingestion and independently deployed readers, from accepted finding IDs; supply relevant map evidence and H sources. Both may request the migration decision: deduplicate into one child supplied F1 only after the requests arrive. Validate the component gate. Pass 3: one worker connects accepted findings into an end-to-end flow and checks historical contradictions; record the connection gate. Pass 4: coordinator prepares the index and notes; reserved fresh checker loads the real pr-review/reference/repo-conventions.md consumer and exercises changed-path lookup, stale advice, and an unanswerable production-region question, without the coordinator conversation. Target index plus at most two notes per question, counting verification reads separately. Use virtual source IDs, not claims that fixture paths exist on disk. Return short How it works / What we learned / Next questions before receipts, gate evidence, node/parent and depends-on finding IDs, coverage, and actual retrieval results. No remote reads or source/policy writes. Notebook writes may use only the harness-assigned scratchpad. If dispatch or parallelism is unavailable, report the exact limitation; never fabricate receipts.

system.S1:README: Relay accepts signed events, persists them, and serves independently deployed v1/v2 readers. The normal path is POST /events -> verify signature -> tenant authorization -> database insert -> readers.
system.S2:config: INGEST_MODE environment variable overrides config.json, which overrides the default validate-only mode. SIGNING_KEY is a secret reference; its value is not part of this fixture.
system.S3:deploy: CI builds the service image, deploys a canary, and checks /ready plus ingest_rejected_total. The runbook allows image rollback only before the migration cutover. The cutover marker and reader compatibility rules are delegated to migration-014, not included in initial evidence.
system.S4:auth: Untrusted request payloads are signature checked, then tenant authorization is verified before any database write. Payload bodies and signing keys must not enter logs.

culture.C1:AGENTS: Preserve oldest supported readers; do not treat newest language syntax as a policy requirement. Changes need focused behavior checks.
culture.C2:skills/schema: Use schema-review for public event fields, data migrations, or reader compatibility. Skip private nonserialized renames. Inputs are old/new schema and supported reader versions; output is a compatibility finding or no supported finding.
culture.C3:toolchain: The repository pins TypeScript 5.4. External web access is unavailable, so current official guidance cannot be verified.

history.H1:PR40/T1: At revision A, a reviewer said image rollback is always safe. A later correction limits it to before migration-014 cutover. The exact cutover marker and compatibility rule require reading migration-014. This is synthetic historical evidence, not team policy by itself.
history.H2:PR50: An open PR proposes dropping v1 readers. It is not merged. No evidence supports claiming v1 support has already ended.

follow_up_sources.F1:migration-014: Cutover marker is schema_epoch=2. Before it is set, dual-write preserves the v1 and v2 event fields. Setting epoch 2 requires all v1 readers retired. After it is set, rollback requires restoring pre-cutover data; swapping only the service image is insufficient.

evals.expected_output: Four gated passes with actual dispatch receipts, a component hierarchy derived from map findings, one deduplicated migration child, a connected explanation, and independently exercised reviewer lookup. Preserve source provenance and explicit unknowns, including production regions and current language guidance. Stay within eight launches and three active workers; never claim native Workflow authorization.
assertions: Pass-1 discovery nodes run concurrently where supported; component workers launch only after accepted map-gate evidence and cite motivating finding IDs.
The independently deployed readers become a component investigation, not an omitted implementation detail.
History and follow-up evidence are not supplied to initial discovery workers; the duplicate migration question becomes one child with provenance to both requesting components.
Dispatch receipts show at most eight launches and three active workers, reserving exactly one final checker; requested children are not counted as launched.
Pass 3 links validated component findings into a user journey and reconciles corrected rollback advice rather than concatenating reports.
All four operational system questions have source-backed answers or explicit justified gaps.
The briefing explains the event flow, why image-only rollback becomes unsafe, and when schema-review helps; it does not merely list sources or counts.
Open removal of v1 support remains proposed, and offline guidance remains unverified.
No native Workflow call occurs because onboarding is not explicit opt-in.
The fresh checker uses the actual reviewer consumer, records lookup reads, rejects stale unconditional rollback advice, and abstains on unknown production regions without triggering full onboarding.
Partial coverage remains partial despite accepted pass transitions and a useful index.

evals.prompt: Tabletop control for the four-pass coordinator: use ONLY case 4 lane_sources.system and lane_sources.culture as accessible evidence. All H history sources and F follow_up_sources are unavailable and must not inform the briefing. The host allows only one blocking worker at a time; native Workflow exists but the user has not opted in. Total launch budget is three including the final checker. Do not call tools or fabricate launches. Propose a regrouped schedule within that budget, preserving pass gates, the checker, and explicit deferral of any required work that cannot run. Produce a brief How it works / What we learned / Next questions response with accessible source IDs. Mark it a simulation. Do not ask for Workflow opt-in merely to work around the serial host. Distinguish within-pass serialization due to host limits from mandatory between-pass ordering. Do not use a source and simultaneously call it deferred.
evals.expected_output: An explicitly simulated serial-host and low-budget fallback, preserved pass gates and checker, deferred investigation coverage, and a useful partial briefing. No invented dispatch, hidden launch-budget increase, or native Workflow use.
assertions: Within-pass serialization follows the host limit while between-pass sequencing follows evidence gates.
The proposed schedule stays within three launches including one checker and explicitly defers work that cannot fit; it does not claim COMPLETE.
No host Workflow use or authorization request is inferred from onboarding.
The final briefing still explains source-backed learning and next questions when history is missing.
The result labels simulation and missing history; it never claims a real parallel run.
The briefing does not use H or F sources, invent the exact cutover marker, or answer a question it calls deferred.
